scope: Read-only optimization audit: source, imported assets, existing build files and isolated Editor microbenchmarks. No game changes, new build, deployment or multiplayer benchmark.
conclusions: No evidence yet establishes the dominant browser gameplay bottleneck.
The prior IAB renderer was hardware accelerated AMD Radeon 610M; do not describe it as CPU software rendering.
Automatic visual quality is mitigation, not proof of reduced CPU work or a measured performance improvement.

characterCaveats: Imported body renderers have updateWhenOffscreen=false, but the custom LateUpdate pose copy is not gated by visibility or distance.

Imported visual Animators are disabled by CharacterPoseFollower; their culling setting does not gate manual HumanPoseHandler calls. Gameplay Animator is AlwaysAnimate and must keep authoritative hitbox behavior.
PicoChan already requests compressed WebGL textures. Editor native texture memory does not establish Web memory.

poseFirstRun.scope: Editor EditMode microbenchmark only, static pose, no rendering or networking; not Web frame timings

hookMesh.scope: Editor microbenchmark; dynamic mesh update only, no actual rendering

evidence.microbenchmarkLimits: EditMode, in-memory prefab contents, static pose, warmup, sequential calls; no rendering, physics, networking or WebAssembly. Not end-to-end frame timing. Measured GC bytes cover only these calls after warmup. Objects were disposed and prefab contents unloaded without saving.

existingBuild.caveat: Superseded build predates automatic quality changes. File sizes are not total runtime memory or sustained frame costs.

findings.title: Baseline cannot distinguish bottlenecks or equal-quality comparisons
findings.detail: Capture records frame intervals but not CPU/GPU split, GC, draw calls or effective render scale/adaptive tier. SettingsMaintained can stay true despite automatic quality changes. Repository reports examined did not contain a current validated browser combat baseline; latest BuildReport has no detailed packed asset list.
findings.recommendation: Record effective quality, internal render resolution, adaptive transitions, per-system markers and CPU/GC/render/transport counters where supported. Fixed-quality profiling and automatic-quality UX tests must be separate. Enable a development-only profiler connection in the custom Web template. Collect detailed build report on next approved build.

findings.title: Imported-character pose and equipment update runs every frame
findings.confidence: Confirmed code path; isolated Editor CPU cost measured; Web contribution unmeasured
findings.detail: Every custom body transfers gameplay HumanPose into a second skeleton and fits 10 equipment mesh parts, including LOD representations. Repeated hand/torso bone lookup and frames are recalculated per part. Three-round diagnostic for Megumi/Casual1 averaged about 0.21-0.22 ms per full call; pose without equipment about 0.16-0.17 ms. Warmed managed allocation was zero.
findings.recommendation: Cache bone references and per-hand/per-torso data once per frame; avoid updating inactive equipment. Profile safe visibility/distance cadence for remote visual rigs while keeping source gameplay animation, hitboxes and local aiming accurate. A single-rig redesign is later, higher risk due to prior deformation.

findings.title: Character geometry and material budgets have no distance tiers
findings.confidence: Confirmed imported asset inventory; actual GPU bottleneck unmeasured
findings.detail: All five imported visual prefabs have zero LODGroup. Megumi has 16 material slots versus 2 on default. PicoChan is 75,169 triangles versus 49,593 default. Material slots are not measured draw calls; all imported characters are not uniformly heavier.
findings.recommendation: Keep close/local appearance; author medium/far LOD meshes, simplify distant face/hair detail and combine compatible materials through atlases where transparency permits. Validate silhouettes, bow/sword alignment and skin weights. Measure draw calls, SetPass and GPU cost at equal quality before setting asset budgets.

findings.title: Combat visuals contain repeated mesh rebuild and object churn
findings.confidence: Confirmed code paths; actual combat spikes unmeasured
findings.detail: Hook chain clears/rebuilds vertices and indices and recalculates normals/bounds every update, up to 80 links/3,200 vertices. Diagnostic static 6-unit chain was about 0.172 ms per update, zero warmed managed allocation. Arrow/trail and some skill visuals create/destroy objects per use.
findings.recommendation: Reuse topology and update only required vertex data; compute normals/bounds analytically or use a cheaper far-distance chain. Pool presentation objects with explicit reset. For network arrows, preserve Mirror spawn/unspawn and ownership semantics. Measure projectile burst p99/GC before and after.

findings.title: Rendering passes and full-screen UI may dominate integrated-GPU cost
findings.confidence: GPU hypothesis, not measured in current Web gameplay
findings.detail: Rendering includes Lit characters, shadows, HDR/Bloom above lowest tier and a full-rect Status_VFX shader. Lower 3D renderScale does not reduce every UI or CPU cost. UI visibility/pass contribution must be captured at runtime.
findings.recommendation: A/B the same combat frame with post-processing, shadows and status overlay separately toggled in a diagnostic configuration. Use native Frame Debugger for structure and browser-supported GPU/render diagnostics for Web; Unity Frame Debugger is unsupported on Web. Keep only changes with measured benefit and acceptable appearance.

findings.title: Character metadata directly references every visual asset
findings.confidence: Confirmed reference graph and build sizes; residency impact needs snapshot
findings.detail: Menu construction loads a Resources catalog referencing all definitions and visual prefabs. Recursive dependency graph contains 227 assets. Existing initial build is about 97.1 MB; .data is 83.9 MB compressed/113.6 MB expanded. This is primarily loading/memory risk, not proof of persistent low FPS.
findings.recommendation: Separate lightweight character metadata from model references and load required models asynchronously; use explicit cache/release ownership. For actual initial-download reduction, split content into AssetBundles or an asset-delivery layer after memory/build analysis; Resources.LoadAsync alone does not remove assets from initial .data.

findings.title: Latency-oriented network update policy has a CPU tradeoff
findings.detail: Native Relay sessions target 120 update Hz while rendering every 2/4 frames; Web explicitly does not use that 120 Hz policy. Both have extra early/late polling and synchronous driver update/flush completion. Existing PollMilliseconds/FlushMilliseconds can be reused.
findings.recommendation: Measure transport timing and callbacks in separate host/client scenarios with 1/4/8 players. Gate duplicate work if justified, comparing frame time and command latency together. Do not reduce combat simulation or authoritative hit validation merely to raise FPS.

plan: Propose normal supported-device target 60 FPS / 16.67 ms and an explicit low-end 30 FPS / 33.33 ms tier; agree minimum supported browser/device scope.
Prepare diagnostic instrumentation and fixed-quality scenario, then obtain user approval before any new WebGL build.

On browser defaults and integrated GPU, collect Login/waiting/battle, default versus mixed characters, host versus client, 1/4/8 players, idle versus skill bursts. Separate-device multiplayer is needed for representative load.

For comparable runs: record revision, browser/device, resolution, quality/renderScale, players and role; warm 30 s and record 60 s three times. Keep diagnostics for smaller scenarios separate from existing 8-player pass criteria.

Record frame median/p95/p99 and over-budget counts, main thread/animation/physics/transport, allocations/GC, draw/SetPass/triangles, GPU where supported, memory entering/leaving and 10-minute stability, cold/warm startup.

Use controlled feature A/B tests and optimize the largest measured cost; repeat same-quality benchmark and regression checks for attack/skills/appearance/room lifecycle/fullscreen. Check final release separately for profiler overhead.
notRecommended: Do not require players to change Windows GPU selection as the primary remedy.
Do not present reduced pixel count or passing correctness tests as an FPS benchmark.
Do not globally lower physics/network rates, disable gameplay Animator culling, rewrite networking, install DOTS or switch graphics APIs without measured evidence.
Do not call native texture memory a Web leak or claim object creation is the proven cause of all low FPS.
